summary: Intermittent GPU handshake timing causing interleaved-burst slot lock and degraded throughput in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed repeated short (10-30s) windows of elevated P99 latency and an immediate drop in sustained throughput from their dedicated pool. Symptoms correlate with many small request bursts that arrive during autoscaler handoff windows. SRE telemetry shows a pattern where GPU "handshake" (attach/detach) operations overlap with local prefetch work and NVLink setup resulting in transient slot locks and batch serialization.

Impact:
- Clip-API (customer live traffic) p95/p99 spiking, downstream user requests failing ~1-3% with 503/504 during bursts.
- Throughput for their dedicated pool fell ~28% during observed windows.
- Customer reports degraded user experience for time-sensitive tasks.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: clipper-prod-dedicated-usw2
- Region: us-west-2
- Node types: A100-40GB mixed with A10X in the same pool (heterogeneous GPU mix)
- Model endpoints: redwood-open-7b (quantized), long-context-8k (FP16)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send many short streams (avg tokens per request ~45) with random inter-arrival jitter of 10-50ms.
2) Run for 20 minutes during autoscaler baseline shrink window (03:00–04:00 UTC).
3) Observe periodic latency spikes and a drop in p50 throughput for the pool.

Observed logs and telemetry snippets:
- Scheduler logs: "attach-req: node-42 pending-prewarm; nvlink-init delayed by 152ms"
- Node-manager: "prefetch-worker busy; handshake-wait queue=6"
- Autoscaler: "scale-down: candidate 3 -> 2 (grace_window=60s)"
- Customer API logs: repeated 503 with "slot-locked-until 2026-03-10T03:12:05Z"

Additional notes:
- Customer claims problem frequency increased after recent autoscaler tuning change (tightened grace_window).
- Heterogeneous GPU mix reported in the pool; scheduling may be attempting cross-type NVLink orchestration causing longer attach times.
investigation:
Initial hypothesis:
- Autoscaler shrink combined with small-stream fanout causes rapid attach/detach churn. When a node is being drained and another is being attached, NVLink and prefetch workers contend for PCIe/NVLink setup time, creating a short window where batchers serialize work to a single slot. This appears like a noisy-neighbor effect but is tied to orchestration timing.

What we checked:
- Correlated cluster events with customer-reported windows (cloud metrics + internal event bus). Found autoscale decisions aligning with observed degradation.
- Reviewed node-level bios and driver logs for thermal throttling: none.
- Verified GPU memory was sufficient; garbage-collection or swap events not present.
- Captured per-node attach/detach duration for the timeframe: median attach=80ms, 95th=420ms (elevated vs baseline 95th=130ms).
- Found increased prefetch-worker CPU saturation on nodes being re-attached (samples show 85-95% CPU on those nodes).

Telemetry links:
- Allocator traces: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/alloc/trace/98a7b3
- Autoscaler events: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/autoscale/events/2026-03-10
comments: 2026-03-10 14:02 - Emma Chen (Support): Initial customer report received. Customer supplied request logs and suggested it started after autoscaler change on 2026-03-08.
2026-03-10 14:30 - Rahul Patel (SRE): Confirmed periodic attach latency. Raised hypothesis about prefetch worker contention during node attach; requested cluster-level attach traces.
2026-03-10 15:10 - Claire Gomez (Infra Eng): Noted heterogeneous GPU mixing in pool. Suggested isolating A100 nodes for the customer to test if NVLink orchestration is contributing.
2026-03-11 09:45 - Emma Chen (Support): Customer agreed to a short A/B: pin traffic to A100-only subpool for 2 hours tomorrow morning (03:00 UTC). Requested rollback plan documented.

2026-03-12 05:20 - Rahul Patel (SRE): A/B test results: A100-only subpool eliminated the brief attach spikes and throughput recovered to baseline. When traffic returned to mixed pool, spikes reappeared. Adding this to evidence for heterogeneity-induced orchestration delays.

2026-03-12 11:00 - Claire Gomez (Infra Eng): Proposed mitigations in PR: prevent autoscaler from shrinking below min_nodes during high small-stream fanout windows; add per-node attach-rate limit; throttle prefetch-workers during attach operations.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Emma Chen (Support): Shared proposed mitigations with customer and scheduled maintenance window for rolling scheduler config change. Customer accepted temporary mitigation and requested post-mortem when resolved.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12):
- Temporarily increased min_nodes for clipper-prod-dedicated-usw2 during peak small-stream windows.
- Deployed autoscaler change: attach-rate-limit=2 nodes/min for mixed pools; grace_window restored to previous setting.
- Added a short pause for prefetch-worker activity during node attach to avoid CPU contention.

Result:
- Throughput returned to within 5% of baseline during a 3-hour verification window. P99 spikes eliminated for A100-only traffic and greatly reduced for mixed pool (from 1.8s to ~220ms).

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Engineering to implement long-term fix in allocator repo to avoid cross-type NVLink orchestration for short-lived attach/detach (PR created: github.com/redwood/realtime-allocator/pull/278).
- Product to propose guidance: recommend dedicated pools avoid mixing GPU families for latency-sensitive small-stream workloads.
- Schedule a postmortem entry in Confluence and update dedicated pool runbook with guidance on autoscaler tuning and attach-rate limits.
- Outreach: Support to send a summary and RCA to Clippr.ai and offer a 1-week monitoring check-in.
root_cause: Transient orchestration contention: attach/detach operations in a heterogeneous dedicated pool led to NVLink/PCIe setup and prefetch-worker CPU contention during autoscaler shrink windows. This caused short-lived slot locks and effective noisy-neighbor-like throughput degradation.
